sections.h2: Where is the Davidson County Register of Deeds and when does it take recordings?
sections.html:
The office is at 110 West Center Street in Lexington, NC 27292, and its mailing address is P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The phone is 336-242-2150 and the fax is 336-238-2318. Doors are open Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm except county holidays, but recording stops promptly at 4:30pm, a rule that took effect August 1, 2020.

The county describes its mission as recording, preserving and giving access to real estate records, vital records and military service records, plus administering the notary oath. Counter visits get same-day recording and same-day return of vital records, and the office offers a public computer lab and self-serve kiosks for legal searches.

sections.h2: How do I search Davidson County land records?
sections.html:
Real estate searches are done online through the county's deeds search site, and records there are indexed from 1984 to the present. For anything earlier than 1984, the office asks you to contact staff directly.

  • When looking for a satisfaction of a mortgage, search under the document type Release.
  • Judgments are checked through the Clerk of Courts office, not the Register of Deeds.
  • Attorneys are encouraged to use an e-record system or submit by mail.
  • Color-coded plats do not upload properly and will not be recorded.

The office also lists answers to common questions on whether an instrument must be notarized, whether you can prepare your own deed and whether you must be present to record.

sections.h2: What is the Davidson County tax certification rule for deeds?
sections.html:
Since March 1, 2019, the Register of Deeds will not accept a deed transferring real property unless the Tax Administrator has certified that no delinquent taxes are a lien on the parcel. The county adopted the requirement by commissioner resolution on August 14, 2018, under G.S. 161-31.

There is one shortcut. A deed submitted under the supervision of a closing attorney is accepted without the certificate if it carries a statement that the instrument was prepared by a North Carolina attorney and that any delinquent taxes will be paid by the closing attorney to the county tax collector from the closing proceeds. Without an attorney, you request a certificate from the Tax Department through its online form, and the county warns that a certificate can take up to two business days. A seller doing a direct sale should start that request before the closing date, since an unpaid prior-year bill will stop the deed at the counter.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Davidson County?
sections.html:
Davidson County follows the uniform fees North Carolina sets by statute. The table shows the state schedule alongside two charges the county prints on its own page.

Recording charges that apply at the Davidson County Register of Deeds
ItemAmountWhere it comes from
Instrument in general$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationNo feeG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Assumed business name filing$26.00Davidson County Register of Deeds page
Card payments3% convenience fee or $1 minimumDavidson County Register of Deeds page

The deed excise tax is separate: the state charges $1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the consideration, and the transferor pays it to the register of deeds before recording.

sections.h2: Does recording protect a Davidson County buyer and seller?
sections.html:
Yes. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option or lease longer than three years is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value except from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies. Registration order sets priority.

That is why a seller in Lexington, Thomasville, Denton or a rural township should treat recording as the final step and not an afterthought. Ask the closing attorney for the recorded book and page, and for proof that the prior deed of trust was released.

sections.h2: Who owes the property tax bill when a Davidson County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The tax collector bills whoever is the listing owner on January 1, and the county says a sale during the year does not erase the seller's liability for that bill. Taxes are usually prorated at closing, so check your settlement statement to see whether the buyer's share was credited.

Sellers who want certainty can ask that the tax collector be paid directly out of closing funds. The tax collector's phone number is 336-242-2180, and the same office handles the tax certifications the Register of Deeds requires. Because a certificate and a recorded deed depend on each other, a seller who clears the tax account first usually avoids a delay at the recording counter.

sections.h2: How big is the Davidson County housing market?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 180,182 residents for July 1, 2025, up 6.7 percent from the April 2020 base, in 79,412 housing units. Land area is 553.18 square miles, and 74.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024.

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing units: $219,100.
  • Median gross rent: $901.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,355.
  • Households: 69,846, averaging 2.45 people.
  • Persons 65 and over: 20.8 percent.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 1,216.

About 92.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Those figures describe the whole county, not a single town.

sections.h2: What other records does the Davidson County office handle?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the office takes military discharges and assumed business name filings by mail at P.O. Box 464, and sellers who are heirs often need its vital records too. Marriage license applications are online, and the applicant then calls to schedule an appointment. A marriage license is valid for 60 days only.

Funeral homes with escrow accounts send certificate requests by fax, and orders are mailed within 48 hours. Others bring the request with payment and proof of their funeral home status, or mail it with a self-addressed stamped envelope. Heirs selling a parent's house usually need a death certificate for the estate file, so ordering a few early saves a second trip.

sections.h2: What should a Davidson County seller do before the deed goes in?
sections.html:
Work through a short list in order:

  • Pull the tax bill for the parcel and see whether anything is delinquent.
  • Decide whether an attorney will close the sale or you will request a tax certificate yourself.
  • Confirm the draftsman line and return address on the deed.
  • Arrange payment of the excise tax and filing fee for the same day.
  • Get the loan payoff and a recorded release of the deed of trust.

If the loan is in default, power-of-sale foreclosure is heard before the clerk of superior court, with ten days to file an upset bid after a sale report. Ask the lender for a written payoff figure before you accept any offer.

faqs.q: What time does the Davidson County Register of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 4:30pm sharp, even though the office stays open until 5pm Monday through Friday. The county put that rule in place on August 1, 2020.

faqs.q: Why was my Davidson County deed refused for taxes?
faqs.a: Since March 1, 2019, the office accepts a real property deed only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.

faqs.q: How far back do the online Davidson County land records go?
faqs.a: Records are indexed from 1984 to the present. For earlier records, contact the Register of Deeds office at 336-242-2150.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Davidson County deed?
faqs.a: The seller, called the transferor, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. State law sets it at $1.00 for each $500.00 or fractional part of the consideration.

faqs.q: Can I record documents by mail in Davidson County?
faqs.a: Military discharges and assumed business name filings can be mailed to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The assumed business name fee is $26.00, and a self-addressed stamped envelope is needed for return.
